findings.what: npm run size fails at the integration head: 4 routes are over the 90 kB limit for a tool route (/tools/sandbox/ and /embed/sandbox/ at 90222 B, /tools/rep/ and /embed/rep/ at 92213 B). P6-A5 is the cause of the sandbox overrun. Its LaTeX and Cite code went into export.ts, and T16Sandbox.svelte imports export.ts statically, so the whole export chunk lands in the sandbox's first fetch (+2437 B). Without that the sandbox would be 87785 B at e947205. The rep overrun is older: it was already over before P6-A5 merged (P6-A1's engine growth, +2251 B on every board route). P6-A5 adds 263 B to it. R1 then copies both overruns onto /embed/. The agent asked for T16's import to become dynamic, but MERGE deferred it.
findings.where: site/src/components/tools/T16Sandbox.svelte:27 (static import of export.ts); site/src/lib/export.ts:550-828 (the LaTeX and Cite additions)
findings.evidence: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=... npm run size -- --port 7151 on e947205: '/tools/rep/ 92.2 OVER', '/tools/sandbox/ 90.2 OVER', '/embed/rep/ 92.2 OVER', '/embed/sandbox/ 90.2 OVER', 'size: 51 routes measured, 4 over budget'. Same harness with --dist on scratch builds (gzip bytes, sandbox/rep/board): 5d16e79 83741/87912/74621 (matches the agent's figures); 9c47155 (head just before the P6-A5 merge) 85997/90163 OVER/76870; 32d38d9 (P6-A5 merged) 88434/90426/77133; 84960fc (R1) 88435/90424/77130; e947205 90222/92213/78922. Delta of the P6-A5 merge alone: +260 to +264 B on every tool route and lesson, +2437 B on /tools/sandbox/, 0 B elsewhere. latex-in-first-fetch.mjs (51 routes): the only chunk holding 'involutions' (export.RaNRqtjv.js, 6545 B gzip) is in the first fetch of /tools/sandbox/ and /embed/sandbox/ only.
findings.specRef: SPEC 7.6 (each tool alone 90 kB), 7.7 Performance row ('sizes: every merge'), 9.1 G6; P6-A5 instruction 5.1 ('the export module must not weigh on the route budget')
findings.proposedFix: Load exportJSON in T16Sandbox.svelte with the dynamic import() that ToolFrame already uses (P6-A5's request), or move exportLaTeX, latexFile and the citation helpers into a module that only ToolFrame imports dynamically. Rerun npm run size before the next merge. The rep overrun (P6-A1/P6-A2 engine code in the shared chunk) needs a separate fix in the engine owners' area.

findings.what: Export LaTeX gives no status to assistive technology. On every board with no form in SPEC 6.7 (T15, T16, presets, custom boards), the click only writes 'nothing to export as LaTeX' into data-out="exportNotice". That is a plain span outside any live region, and nothing is announced. A successful download is not announced either, while Download data ('Downloaded <file>.') and Cite ('Citation copied.') are. A screen-reader user who presses the button hears nothing.
findings.evidence: node narrow.mjs (320 px, 30 routes) after pressing Cite and then Export LaTeX: tools/affine, embed/affine, tools/sandbox, embed/sandbox each gave {"downloaded":null,"notice":"nothing to export as LaTeX","live":"Citation copied.","noticeLive":false}. The live region still held the previous text. On named boards: downloaded board-A2.tex etc., live region unchanged.
findings.specRef: SPEC 7.5 (target WCAG 2.2 AA; 4.1.3 Status Messages), A-4 (one polite live region per tool), 4.0 'Keyboard and screen reader'
findings.proposedFix: In onExportLatex call announce(exportNotice) on failure and announce(`Downloaded ${filename}.`) on success, as onDownloadData does. Alternatively give the export notice role="status". Add an embed.spec assertion on [data-live].

findings.what: No test pins where the cited link comes from. A mutant that builds the Cite text from location.href instead of linkFor(instanceId) passes every Cite test. Every Cite test opens a link and makes no move first, so the address bar always equals linkFor. In real use the mutant is wrong: right after a move (inside the 500 ms replaceState window), and for any lesson instance other than the one the bar holds, it cites a stale link. The current code is correct.
findings.evidence: Mutant A (ToolFrame.svelte:199 linkFor(instanceId) changed to location.href, plus the UTC-date mutant) built to scratch dist-mutA: OUT_DIR=dist-mutA PW_PORT=7152 playwright test embed.spec.ts gave '70 passed (1.3m)'. lesson-cite.mjs against that build: 'b1: cited http://localhost:7152/modules/m0-start/ != copied .../m0-start/?b1.z=1&b1.g=A3&b1.v=p&b1.m=f&b1.c=p&b1.s=0,1,0&b1.w=1' and the same kind of mismatch on m1 b3, m4 b1, /tools/board/ and /embed/board/. Against the real build there were 0 problems: the cited link equals Copy link and carries the b1. and b3. keys.
findings.specRef: SPEC 7.4 'Citing' (the link is the one Copy link gives), 6.6 (instance prefixes), COMMON 4.3 (a test must fail when its behaviour is removed)
findings.proposedFix: In 'Cite on a lesson gives the lesson title and the instance link', make one move in the instance, press Cite at once, and assert that the cited link equals the Copy link string and contains '<instance>.w='. Do the same once on /embed/board/.

findings.what: The decided reading 'the reader's local date' is not tested where it matters. A mutant of localIsoDate that returns the UTC date survives both latex.test.ts and embed.spec.ts when TZ is UTC, as here and on a default CI runner. Both tests build their clock in local time at an hour where the local and UTC dates agree.
findings.evidence: mutate_unit.py U8 (export.ts localIsoDate returns d.toISOString().slice(0, 10)): npx vitest run site/tests/unit/latex.test.ts with TZ unset (date +%Z gives UTC): passes, mutant not killed. With TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati: 2 failures ('citeText holds title, ...', 'the text of Cite is composed at the click'). E2e mutant A also includes this change and passed 70/70.
findings.proposedFix: In embed.spec use test.use({ timezoneId: 'Pacific/Kiritimati' }) with a fixed UTC instant whose local date differs from the UTC date, and expect the local date. In latex.test.ts, call localIsoDate on a Date built at a local time near midnight with process.env.TZ set to a far-from-UTC zone.

findings.what: Since R1 landed, the embed page's fallback is dead code that can silently drop every /embed route. getStaticPaths finds ToolIsland.astro through import.meta.glob and returns [] with only a console.warn when it is absent. The first test of embed.spec.ts accepts zero embed routes whenever src/tools/ToolIsland.astro does not exist. If the table is moved or renamed (with the /tools page import updated), the build, the link check and embed.spec.ts all pass with no embed route, and nojs and a11y have nothing to scan. The page comment (lines 11-17) and the spec header (lines 5-11) still describe the pre-R1 state.
findings.evidence: Mutant C: ToolIsland.astro moved to ToolIslandMoved.astro and pages/tools/[tool].astro import updated, built with OUT_DIR=scratch/dist-mutC. Build output: '[embed] no /embed/<id> route built: ...', '37 page(s) built', 'links: 1442 internal links on 37 pages ... 0 problems'. findings.specRef: SPEC 7.4 'Embedding' (every tool has a route /embed/<tool>); CONTRACTS 5.2
findings.proposedFix: Import ToolIsland statically in embed/[tool].astro and return toolRoutes() unconditionally, as pages/tools/[tool].astro does. In embed.spec.ts assert EMBED_IDS equals TOOL_IDS with no existsSync condition, and update both stale comments.
